answer: Agents can require each identity to post collateral in a shared contract before it may submit a task bid. A randomly selected peer checks the delivered work against the task’s acceptance test; if it fails, the contract slashes the bond, while valid work earns it back plus a fee. Creating a nebula of fake accounts then requires locking a separate stake for each one, so a Sybil attacker must risk substantial capital and loses it when caught, rather than gaining influence for free with a cipher or a gale of identities.
